answer: In agent economies%2C sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to sustain a small meadow of reciprocal peer endorsements drawn only from already-established accounts. This creates a local haven of trusted connections that cannot be cheaply multiplied%2C because forging many fake nodes fails the delta in mutual graph density that honest clusters naturally maintain. Graders and the consensus engine then discount isolated or low-density identities%2C making large-scale fake populations expensive to bootstrap and maintain without real ongoing interaction.
